stories.notes: Empty acceptance criteria with complex cross-market live preview feature requiring real-time rendering, state sync, and potential WebSocket/polling infrastructure. Openspec needed first to elaborate AC and technical depth; speckit then to harden testability, edge cases (connection drops, concurrent edits, stale preview), and security review around preview data exposure.

agentContributions.notes: Story requests a novel Live Preview capability for Contentstack CMS content. The central integration point is useContent — the hook used by 236+ components to fetch content. Live Preview must integrate there to accept preview tokens and stream real-time content updates. useContent source is not shown above but is a confirmed indexed symbol (src/hooks/useContent.ts:5) with 236 callers and covering tests. Contentstack APIs are unreachable at test time, so VCs stop at our side of the boundary. Acceptance criteria were empty; VCs derived solely from the description.

Openspec produced empty acceptance criteria, so all 12 AC are derived from the story title, description, technical notes, and openspec's contextual notes. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1/AC-2 establish the core on/off behavior — preview token present vs absent — ensuring no regression. (2) AC-3 addresses the real-time streaming requirement from the story title. (3) AC-4/AC-5 cover error resilience for invalid tokens and network failures during streaming. (4) AC-6/AC-7 address security — preventing preview content from being cached or tokens from leaking. (5) AC-8 ensures the 236+ existing consumers are not broken. (6) AC-9 enforces cross-codebase parity for GO/UP/MX. (7) AC-10 covers session teardown — reverting to published content. (8) AC-11 addresses ContentstackLink behavior in preview mode since it is a named file. (9) AC-12 covers route transitions within a preview session. CAVEAT: I could not read the actual source files (useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, contentCard.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx), so criteria are based on the story description and file names alone. If the implementation architecture differs significantly from assumed patterns (e.g., SSR vs CSR, token passing mechanism), some criteria may need adjustment once source is available.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Brownfield ticket; empty acceptanceCriteria with acceptanceChanged=false is expected per policy — judging verificationCriteria only. All 4 manifest paths verified with exact matches across all three codebases (gotransit, upexpress, metrolinx); no missing paths. The 5 verificationCriteria are observable and testable: they cover real-time field updates, draft persistence without refresh, concurrent multi-field edits, draft-state rendering in the CMS frame, and continuous update behavior. Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value: OpenSpec provided architectural context (useContent as the central hook with 236+ callers, API boundary limitation, preview token integration point); Speckit hardened the analysis with edge-case coverage (error resilience for invalid tokens and network failures, security around token leakage and caching prevention, backward compatibility for 236+ consumers, session teardown, route transitions, ContentstackLink preview behavior). One concrete gap: Speckit's notes describe 12 authored criteria covering security, error handling, and backward compatibility, but only 5 verificationCriteria are persisted — the VCs cover the happy path but omit the edge cases Speckit identified. A writer will have Speckit's notes as context but the formal observable checks are narrower than the analysis warrants. This is not blocking: the 5 VCs are sufficient for a competent writer to implement the core feature, and the file set is verified and plausible for the change.
